Counts number doctor visits often overdispersed: variance larger mean, Poisson model allow. often also contain zeros Poisson (even negative binomial) distribution predicts. negative binomial (NB2) model handles overdispersion dispersion parameter θ\theta. zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) model also allows separate process produces “structural” zeros. nbzinbKoo package fits models algorithms written scratch: iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) alternated Newton–Raphson NB regression, EM algorithm whose M-steps IRLS fits ZINB regression. call optim() general-purpose optimizer. report describes methods (Section 2) package (Section 3), checks results MASS::glm.nb() pscl::zeroinfl() (Section 4), studies ZINB estimator simulation (Section 5), analyzes physician office visits NMES1988 data (Section 6).

title: Negative Binomial and Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial Regression by IRLS
text: nbzinbKoo fits negative binomial (NB2) zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) regression models algorithms written scratch, without optim() general-purpose optimizer: nbreg(): IRLS coefficients alternated Newton-Raphson log⁡θ\log\theta (results match MASS::glm.nb() 10−810^{-8}); zinbreg(): EM algorithm whose M-steps weighted logistic IRLS fit (zero part) weighted NB fit (count part), standard errors analytic observed information matrix (results match pscl::zeroinfl() well within 10−310^{-3}). Website project report: https://gracko95.github.io/nbzinbKoo/ STA 651 (Categorical Data Analysis) final project, Miami University, Fall 2026.

what: Zero-inflated negative binomial regression by EM with IRLS M-steps — zinbreg
title: Zero-inflated negative binomial regression by EM with IRLS M-steps — zinbreg
text: Fits ZINB model $$P(Y_i = 0) = \pi_i + (1-\pi_i) f_{NB}(0;\mu_i,\theta), \qquad       P(Y_i = y) = (1-\pi_i) f_{NB}(y;\mu_i,\theta),\ y \ge 1,$$ \(\log\mu_i = x_i^\top\beta + o_i\) (count model) \(\mathrm{logit}\,\pi_i = z_i^\top\gamma\) (zero-inflation model), EM algorithm: E-step: \(\tau_i = \pi_i / \{\pi_i + (1-\pi_i) f_{NB}(0;\mu_i,\theta)\}\) \(y_i = 0\), else \(\tau_i = 0\). M-step, zero part: logistic IRLS fractional response \(\tau_i\). M-step, count part: NB fit nbreg() prior weights \(a_i = 1 - \tau_i\).
